title: Several Hotel Reservations Held at Once by One Guest
content:
A guest may hold any number of hotel reservations at the same time, including several at the same property on overlapping dates, and each reservation carries its own rate plan from the Hotel Rate Plans range and its own folio. There is no ceiling on the number of reservations one guest may hold.

**Where two reservations meet.** Where two reservations at the same property overlap in dates and name the same lead guest, the later reservation is opened and then referred for duplicate review, because properties treat duplicate rooms as a single guarantee. The match that gives rise to that review is a match of property, of dates and of lead guest together.

**Rooms and rate plans stay where they are.** Rooms are never moved between reservations: a guest who wants fewer rooms cancels the rooms on the reservation they stand on, and each room follows that reservation's own rate plan. Rate plans are never mixed on one reservation; a guest who wants different terms for different rooms holds two reservations.

**The same rules put as questions.** *May one guest hold four reservations at one property for the same week?* Yes — no limit is set on how many reservations a guest holds, and each is opened on its own terms; where the property, the dates and the lead guest coincide, the later of any two is referred for duplicate review. *May two rooms on one reservation sit on different plans of the Hotel Rate Plans range?* No: one reservation carries one rate plan, and different terms for different rooms mean two reservations. *May a room be moved from one reservation to another to reduce a party?* No: the rooms given up are cancelled on the reservation they stand on.
